name: Law
notice: Study material, not legal advice. The law is stated for England and Wales unless a lesson says otherwise; Scotland and Northern Ireland differ (School 17). Completing a LawGradify course is not a legal qualification and does not authorise you to practise. Law changes: check current sources before you rely on anything here.

paths.name: LLB: the foundations of legal knowledge
paths.sub: The core of a qualifying law degree in England and Wales, in the order most universities teach it.

paths.name: Graduate Diploma in Law (conversion)
paths.sub: The seven foundation subjects for non-law graduates, compressed into one year, with the skills to study them.

paths.name: SQE1 · FLK1
paths.sub: Business Law and Practice, Dispute Resolution, Contract, Tort, the Legal System, Constitutional and Administrative Law, EU Law and Legal Services, with ethics throughout. 180 single-best-answer questions.

paths.name: SQE1 · FLK2
paths.sub: Property Practice, Wills and the Administration of Estates, Solicitors' Accounts, Land Law, Trusts, and Criminal Law and Practice, with ethics throughout. 180 single-best-answer questions.

paths.name: SQE2: practical legal skills
paths.sub: Interviewing and attendance notes, advocacy, case and matter analysis, research, writing and drafting, in the five practice contexts, with realistic case files.

paths.name: Preparing for the Bar
paths.sub: Academic preparation for barristers: legal foundations, criminal and civil advocacy, evidence, procedure, opinion writing, drafting, conference skills and ethics. This is study, not Bar training.

paths.name: Law across the UK
paths.sub: What changes in Scotland and Northern Ireland: courts, legislatures, contract, delict, crime, property, succession and qualification.

paths.name: Postgraduate and advanced study
paths.sub: The public, international and theoretical subjects LLM and research students build on.

paths.name: Understanding the law
paths.sub: For anyone curious about how law works: what it is, who makes it, how courts decide and what rights you have.

exams.title: SQE1 FLK1 practice: 45 questions

interactives.title: Okoye v Harbour Cameras: was there a contract?
interactives.sub: Identify the issues, apply offer, acceptance and the postal rule to a sequence of messages, and advise the client, building an IRAC analysis as you go.
interactives.note: A fictional case file on offer and acceptance in the law of England and Wales, with simplified facts and scored decisions; study material, not legal advice.

interactives.title: Court hierarchy and precedent
interactives.sub: Explore the courts of England and Wales and decide whether earlier decisions bind, persuade or must be taken into account.
interactives.note: The court hierarchy of England and Wales and the general rules of precedent; exceptions are summarised, not exhaustive.
